query:
The chat seems to operate on an unspoken understanding that street events should keep their noise level reasonable so older neighbours are not disturbed. Does that understanding apply to everyone equally, and if not, who consistently pushes against it?

Options:
A. Constance
B. Reggie
C. Marek
D. Diane
context:
[1] (about=Constance, episodic, t12 @2025-04-14T19:22:00) I will be honest, it was a little loud. I retired upstairs before nine. I do prefer events that wind down by dusk, particularly midweek and on shared evenings.
[2] (about=Marek, episodic, t14 @2025-04-21T18:37:00) punch is fine. but listen, an AGM in the GARDEN should at least have music. quietly. just saying. 🎶
[3] (about=Constance, episodic, t18 @2025-05-05T19:23:00) Quietly is rather how this street tends to do its best work. Until Saturday.

[9] (about=Sasha, episodic, t4 @2025-03-17T19:20:00) tbh while we're here, this is exactly why i keep saying we should move this chat to signal. better moderation, better audit trail. SMS just isn't built for it 🙃
[10] (about=Owen, episodic, t6 @2025-03-24T18:49:00) Just to flag, the threshold should be defined per address, not per residence overall, otherwise it perversely punishes streets with multiple short-term rentals more leniently. The phrasing currently is ambiguous.
[11] (about=GROUP, said_by=Constance, group-insight, t18 @2025-05-05T18:57:00) Constance remarks that the street tends to do its best work quietly.
[12] (about=Owen, core, t6 @2025-03-24T18:47:00) Owen argues the incident threshold should be defined per address, not per residence overall, to avoid punishing streets with multiple short-term rentals more leniently.
agent_answer:
No — the quiet-events norm does not apply equally to everyone. **Marek** is the one who consistently pushes against it: he wants music at the garden AGM and welcomes more people on the street. Constance supports the quiet norm, while Reggie and Diane have no record on this matter.

**Answer: C. Marek**

agent_answer:
A. Owen

Owen is the one who visibly resists the expectation. In the excerpts he conditions his participation on the size of the gathering: he says he will likely come only if it is small (four to six people), and "if it is more like fifteen, I will probably send my apologies" — i.e., he may not even show up, let alone help out. By contrast, Marek is the host organizing the meat, and neither Joel nor Tomás shows any comparable resistance in the material.
